subject: GPU pool preemption: backfill & temporary SLA bridge proposal
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@brightedge.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightedge.ai
Date: 2027-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Unplanned throughput degradation impacting model endpoints — immediate help needed

Hi Rafael,

We started seeing a sustained throughput drop across our prod inference endpoints at ~08:50 PT this morning. Latency jumped from our baseline 120ms to 700-1,200ms and token throughput dropped ~60% for ~30 minutes — several user transactions timed out. Our on-call traced it to a couple of warmed-up dedicated GPU nodes losing capacity due to preemption and subsequent autoscale lag.

Quick details:
- Affected endpoints: bex/resp-qa-v2, insights/embedder-v1
- Error surface: 502/timeout spikes, 5xx on retries, increased queue depth in our client
- Customer impact: live product sessions delayed; demo scheduled for 10:00 AM impacted

We need immediate mitigation and a written plan for remediation and credits. Please advise:
1) Can you route our traffic to hosted fallback pools temporarily (we need <150ms p95)?
2) What’s the timeline for backfilling capacity and preventing preemptions?
3) We will need a formal proposal for credits / SLA bridge for today’s impact to share with procurement.

Attaching snippets of timing charts and a heap of client-side logs.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of ML Ops
BrightEdge Analytics

Attachment stubs: timing-chart-08-50.png (image), client-logs-08-52.txt (text)

Subject: Re: Unplanned throughput degradation impacting model endpoints — immediate help needed

Samir — thanks for the data and the quick heads-up. We’re treating this as high priority.

Short answers up front:
- We can route a subset of your traffic to our hosted pools within ~10–12 minutes; that will reduce latency but may change billing profile.
- We’re assembling a targeted backfill plan for the affected dedicated pool (pool ID: ded-pool-us-west-9) and will propose an SLA bridge/credit in writing by EOD tomorrow.

Immediate actions I’ve kicked off:
- Marissa (AM) is looping in accounts/ops to approve hosted routing for the demo window.
- Neha (Support Lead) is pulling the orchestration logs and GPU host telemetry; she’ll share the first diagnostics set within the hour.
- I’ve asked infra to set a temporary anti-preemption guard on two reserved nodes while we backfill.

Please confirm if you want us to enable hosted fallback now for the 10:00 demo. If yes, we’ll do a targeted path split (10–20% initially) and monitor p95 for 5–10 minute intervals.

— Rafael
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Operational plan (short):
1) Approve hosted fallback for the duration of the demo (10:00–11:00 PT). Routing to be 15% -> 35% if p95 improves.
2) Infra to hold two reserved nodes (anti-preempt) for 4 hours as a temporary stabilizer.
3) Support to produce initial diagnostics (orchestration logs, node-level GPU telemetry, eviction traces). Neha to own.
4) Accounts to prepare a two-part proposal: (A) immediate SLA bridge (one-day credit + operational credit if p95 > 250ms for >15 min) and (B) 30-day action plan with capacity backfill timings and config changes (preemption guard, autoscale tuning, proactive warm standbys).

Approvals needed:
- Rafael: confirm hosted routing and anti-preempt guard
- Finance/AM (Marissa): ok to offer one-day service credit + expedited procurement paperwork for permanent reserved nodes upgrade if BrightEdge signs commit

I’ll draft the formal bridge/proposal and attach cluster diagnostics once Neha posts them. Rafael — want me to send the proposal directly to procurement@brightedge.ai or to you first?

Date: 2027-02-22T16:34:00-08:00
Subject: Bridge proposal and follow-up: BrightEdge GPU pool preemption incident (20 Feb)

Samir / Procurement team — thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Below is the agreed remediation plus formal proposal attached.

What happened (concise):
- A subset of dedicated nodes in ded-pool-us-west-9 were preempted by the cloud provider during a maintenance window that overlapped our autoscale policy. Our autoscaler reacted but the warm-standby count and reconcilers were insufficient to recover to baseline within the 30-minute window. We have a root-cause ticket in infra (INC-4871).

Immediate remediation completed:
- Temporary hosted fallback enabled at 10:02 PT for the demo; p95 reduced to ~130ms.
- Two nodes pinned with anti-preempt guard for 4 hours; warm-standby counts increased.
- Autoscale tuning: backoff reduced and proactive rewarm threshold added.

Proposal (attached PDF):
- One business-day service credit for 20 Feb incident (applied as 100% of one day of dedicated capacity costs)
- Operational credit: additional 25% service credit if p95 for any affected endpoint exceeds 250ms for >15 minutes in the next 30 days
- We will execute the 30-day backfill and hardening plan in the attached schedule (milestones and point owners included).

Attachments: bridge-proposal-BrightEdge-20270222.pdf, cluster-diagnostics-20270220.tar.gz, procurement-form-filled.pdf

Next steps:
1) Procurement — please confirm receipt and we’ll route the proposal to your finance lead for countersignature.
2) Ops — Neha will post the first diagnostics bundle to the shared drive and the infra ticket INC-4871 will get the priority label.
3) Rafael / Marissa — we’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up on Feb 24 to review the 30-day plan. 

If you want any changes to the credit calculus or the schedule, tell us and we’ll update the PDF.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
